The two classes would be (1) recreational type NPA's with off-road capabilities and (2) all other NPA's. Because of the uncertainty of the final resolution of these issues, the Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) describes the impact of a range of possible final fuel economy requirements and includes a provision for the two classes. Based on the comments to the Notice of Proposed Rulemaking and information already in the agency's possession, the NHTSA has concluded that the final standard will be between 16.4 mpg and 18.7 mpg. If a separate classification is established for four-wheel drive recreational vehicles, the NHTSA has concluded that the standard for that class of vehicles will be between 14.9 and 17.4 mpg. Fuel economy will be determined in accordance with procedures established by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).
••••
The AFES is based on the manufacturers' voluntary product plans for MY 1979. The AFES is so based in order to avoid causing or aggravating a shift in the NPA market towards heavier, less fuel economical vehicles more than 6,000 pounds GVWR and less than 10,000 pounds GVWR, which are not subject to the AFES.
